warning: Development-only research model. No new independent holdout evaluation or clinical validation.
target_description: Post-study revised UCLA 20-item total; 10 positive items reversed including Q4.
selection: Lowest mean 5-fold development CV MAE; nested CV separately estimates the selection procedure.
evaluation: 5 outer participant folds; 4 inner folds for selection. All preprocessing fitted inside folds.
importance_method: Out-of-fold permutation importance for the development-selected configuration; exploratory, not an independent attribution audit.

provenance.target: Post-study revised UCLA 20-item total; 10 positive items reversed including Q4.

features.label: Reported exercise frequency
features.description: Share of observed exercise-report days with a Yes response to vigorous exercise. Self-report, not sensor-derived exercise minutes.

features.label: Change in reported sleep
features.unit: hours: second half minus first half
features.description: Mean sleep in days 15–28 minus days 1–14; at least three observed days in each half. Negative means less sleep later.

features.label: Day-to-day conversation variation
features.description: Sample SD of detected conversation minutes across event-days. Not a measure of total social interaction.

features.label: Change in detected conversation
features.unit: minutes: second half minus first half
features.description: Second-half minus first-half mean, with three recorded event-days per half. Negative means less detected conversation later; missing event-days are not zeros.

features.label: Day-to-day phone-lock variation
features.description: Sample SD of phone-locked duration across recorded event-days. Not variation in screen-use duration.

features.label: Change in phone-locked duration
features.unit: hours: second half minus first half
features.description: Second-half minus first-half mean of recorded phone-locked hours, requiring three event-days in each half.

features.label: Nighttime phone-locked duration
features.description: Mean recorded locked time between midnight and 06:00, requiring three nights with recorded lock events. This is not nighttime phone-use duration.

limitations: Small single-campus observational cohort; no clinical validation.
Survey table provides pre/post type, not individual completion timestamps. Early four-week window precedes intended end-term survey; exact individual ordering cannot be audited.
Sleep is self-reported EMA, not passive sensing. Left-censored <3-hour responses and invalid codes excluded; this can bias sleep summaries.
Conversation and phone-lock means use days with recorded events only. Missing event-days are not assumed to be zero and complete sensor coverage is unknown.
Detected conversation is not total social time. Locked duration is not screen time.
Only participants with >=7 observed days per channel are included; coverage filtering may introduce selection bias.
Features are four-week averages; single-day user inputs are out of task.
Different target scale from GLOBEM: no pooling or cross-dataset accuracy claim.
Exercise is an active self-report, not passive activity sensing.
Locked duration is not phone-use duration. Nighttime use remains unmeasured.
Conversation change is a change in detected events, not a confirmed drop in social interaction.
Event-day means and changes depend on recording coverage.
Seven reserved participants were excluded before raw feature processing.
No feature selection by outcome correlation, no model retraining, and no new holdout evaluation performed.

shap.scope: Descriptive explanations of the development-fitted Ridge model, not new validation.
shap.reference: Mean of transformed development features; equivalent to full development background for interventional linear SHAP.
limitations: SHAP explains this fitted model; it does not improve its predictive validity.
Interventional attribution breaks feature dependence; correlated inputs can receive different credit under other SHAP assumptions.
These are score-point contributions, not probabilities, diagnoses or causal effects.
Global summaries describe training/development behavior and are not independent performance evidence.
Only aggregate background means are retained in the model artifact; no background participant rows are stored.
